title: Levius
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In an alternate steam-powered 19th century recovering from war, teenage Levius, who lost his arm and whose mother was left unconscious in an attack, fights in Mechanical Martial Arts, a brutal sport of cybernetically enhanced boxers, under his uncle Zacks. His climb through the ranks collides with A.J. Langdon, a young fighter tied to the military corporation Amethyst. The three-volume omnibus continues in Levius/est.
life_message: Asks why people fight: courage and care for family are honored, but war's machinery and guilt-driven heroism carry heavy costs.

content.note: Brutal arena bouts and war backstory (Wikipedia; ANN); AniList Gore 79% and MangaUpdates Blood and Gore, but ANN says no graphic gore, so held at 5 (to verify).
Grim tone, amputation, mother in a vegetative state (ANN; Wikipedia); AniList Tragedy.
Trauma, guilt and a hero complex drive Levius (ANN); MangaUpdates Traumatic Past.

dominant: Why we fight; human cost of war technology; family loyalty

frames.aligns: Levius fights to save his mother; questions dignity of bodies made into weapons.
frames.concerns: Arena violence as spectacle; heroism driven by guilt.

frames.aligns: War's wounds weigh on every fighter.
frames.concerns: Anger and violence fill the ring.

folkways.japan: A European steampunk setting, but the uncle-nephew mentor bond and endurance ethic echo Japanese sports-manga norms.

delivery.evidence: ANN finds the themes of why people fight carried by each fighter's motives, and calls the volume 3 villain generic.

Fighting for ego and admiration of an idol

delivery.note: Different fighters' reasons are compared through their bouts; reviewers note the main villain is less developed.

winners_losers: Levius rises through the ranks at physical cost; the war-profiting Amethyst corporation is the looming threat; sympathy goes to fighters damaged by war.
